To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We propose a novel approach for learning sparse representations that minimize the number of operations required during retrieval, (2) Our method is simple, efficient and easy to implement, (3) Our experiments demonstrate that the learned sparse embeddings are competitive to the other state-of-the-art approaches and achieve similar or better speed-accuracy tradeoffs.

we propose to learn distributed sparse representations via minimizing the number of floating point operations (FLOPS), and our experiments on practical datasets show that our approach yields a similar or improved speed-vs-accuracy performance compared to the state-of-the-art baselines.

we present a novel approach to learning distributed sparse representations that are more efficient than dense representations, and that our proposed approach is competitive to state-of-the-art approaches in terms of retrieval accuracy while yielding a similar or better tradeoff in terms of speed.

learning sparse embeddings that are both efficient for retrieval and effective for representation learning.
developing a novel approach to efficiently learn distributed sparse representations for large-scale retrieval.
the design of sparse representations that can be efficiently retrieved and stored.

our proposed approach is a novel approach for efficient retrieval that is competitive to other baselines and has the advantage of being more flexible in terms of the number of bits used for quantization and the sparsity of the learned embeddings.

The main takeaway from our work is that
learning sparse embeddings can be more effective than learning compact representations for retrieval tasks.
learning distributed sparse representations is an effective and efficient way to reduce the computational cost of retrieval.

the FLOPs incurred during retrieval can be used as a proxy for the computational complexity of retrieval and that minimizing this quantity can be a powerful tool for learning sparse representations for efficient retrieval.
